messages.author: 874be8ee14c3aafd
messages.subject: facet errors
parts:
I'm trying to do a plot like the one below:

data(mpg)
qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars, facets = vs + cyl ~ . )

and am getting this error:

Error in .$scales$y[[i]] : subscript out of bounds

I'm assuming this is because of the missing levels in vs:cyl, since vs
+ am ~ . works. Is this a known limitation or is this a bug for
factors with sparse interactions? Does anyone know of a workaround?

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: facet errors
parts:
On 6/21/2011 12:13 PM, Jason Law wrote:
> I'm trying to do a plot like the one below:
>
> data(mpg)
> qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars, facets = vs + cyl ~ . )
>
> and am getting this error:
>
> Error in .$scales$y[[i]] : subscript out of bounds
>
> I'm assuming this is because of the missing levels in vs:cyl, since vs
> + am ~ . works. Is this a known limitation or is this a bug for
> factors with sparse interactions? Does anyone know of a workaround?

You get the same error if you use the ggplot version of the call:

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=mpg, y=wt)) + geom_point() +
facet_grid(vs + cyl ~ .)
# Error in .$scales$y[[i]] : subscript out of bounds

I'm guessing that you are right about the cause. I didn't know about
the bug, but there is one filed about it

https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/165

As a workaround, you can make sure that the data has every combination,
even if it is missing data and thus will get dropped from the plot (with
a warning):

mtcars2 <- rbind.fill(mtcars,
expand.grid(vs=unique(mtcars$vs), cyl=unique(mtcars$cyl)))
ggplot(mtcars2, aes(x=mpg, y=wt)) + geom_point() +
facet_grid(vs + cyl ~ .)

You get a warning message about every facet removing one row of missing
values, but at least it plots.

--

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: facet errors
parts:
Hi Jason,

What about creating the combined factor manually?

require(ggplot2)

mtcars <- within(mtcars, {
carb <- as.factor(carb)
carb <- reorder(reorder(carb, as.numeric(cyl)), as.numeric(vs))
})

mtcars$mygrid <- apply(mtcars[, c("vs", "cyl")], 1, paste, collapse = '')

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = carb)) +
geom_point(aes(shape = factor(gear), colour = factor(am))) +
facet_grid(mygrid ~ ., space = 'free', scales = 'free_y')

I am sure there are ways to improve the strip labels, but I wanted to
check that that is actually what you want first.

Cheers,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: facet errors
parts:
Josh,

That appears like it may be the only option.  It was my first inclination.  It's nice that ggplot respects the size of the text labels for factors so that you can do:

data(mtcars)
mtcars <- 
  within(mtcars, {
         carb.vs <- interaction(vs, carb, sep = '\n')
         am <- as.factor(am)})

ggplot(data = mtcars, aes(mpg, am)) + geom_point() +
  facet_grid(carb.vs ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = 'free')

Just thought I'd find out if there was something that was less of a hack.

Thanks,

Jason
